newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tyndall confident of higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tyndall confident of higher earnings.

text.p: Financial services group Tyndal Australia ltd managing director Michael Wilkins said on Wednesday the company was confident of achieving higher earnings in calendar 1997.
Asked if he was confident of achieving higher earnings, Wilkins said: "We are not giving out predictions, but yes we are looking for an increase."

Wilkins said Tyndall expected that funds management and insurance group, Oceanic Capital Holdings Ltd, which it acquired in January, would contribute to the group's profitability. "We see growth in our other business areas as well," he said.
Tyndall earlier said its net profit for calendar 1996 rose 29.2 percent to A$22.07 million.
Wilkins said because of the variability of financial markets Tyndall had a stated objective to achieve average profit growth of 15 percent between 1990 and the year 2000.
"Thus far we have achieved that and then some," he said.
Wilkens said the only factor that could stop Tyndall performing better in 1997 was if investment markets turned sour.
"Certainly we have backed away from the equities market quite substantially compared to where we were last year," he said.
Wilkins said in terms of the group's market to market funds, the equity component was now about 55 percent compared to 75 percent at the same time last year.
Tyndall was in a good position to take advantage of expected further rationalisation in Australia's financial services industry, Wilkins said.
The company earlier announced a one-for-10 rights issue to raise A$24.3 million to retire debt and provide flexibility in developing the core businesses of the group.
Wilkins said no more than A$15 million of the funds raised would be used to retire debt.

Tyndall was always looking at acquisition opportunities, Wilkins said, but the company would not comment on rumours that it was looking at acquiring NZI Life from British insurer General Accident Plc.
"If we have something to announce we will certainly do that," he said.
Tyndall shares closed three cents firmer at A$1.98.
